specimen_type: Liver, ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a hepatic mass

sections.Clinical details: A 62-year-old man presented with weight loss. No primary tumour is known. Imaging showed multiple hepatic lesions, and an ultrasound-guided core biopsy was requested to establish the diagnosis.
sections.Specimen: Liver, ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a hepatic mass. Fixed in 10% neutral buffered formalin.
sections.Gross description: Two cores of pale tan tissue, measuring 1.4 cm and 1.1 cm in length and approximately 0.2 cm in diameter. The entire specimen is submitted in two cassettes.
sections.Microscopic description: Sections show hepatic parenchyma infiltrated by a poorly differentiated malignant epithelial neoplasm arranged in sheets, trabeculae and nests. No gland formation or mucin is seen, and the tumour cells show keratinisation and intercellular bridges. Tumour cells have pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei with prominent nucleoli and scant to moderate cytoplasm. Mitotic figures are frequent and there is geographic necrosis. The tumour infiltrates between hepatocytes, and entrapped hepatocytes are seen at the periphery.
sections.Immunohistochemistry:
CK7: positive
CK20: negative
TTF-1: positive
Napsin A: positive
CDX2: negative
HepPar-1: negative
sections.Diagnosis: Liver, ultrasound-guided core biopsy: metastatic poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma infiltrating liver parenchyma. The immunophenotype supports a pulmonary primary.
sections.Synoptic summary:
Tumour size: Not applicable
Histologic grade: Poorly differentiated (G3)
Margins: Not applicable
Lymphovascular invasion: Not applicable
Perineural invasion: Not applicable
Lymph nodes (positive/total): Not applicable
pT: Not applicable
pN: Not applicable
Staging edition: AJCC 8th edition
sections.Comment: The immunohistochemical profile (CK7 positive, TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, CK20 negative, CDX2 negative, HepPar-1 negative) supports a lung primary. The primary site is not confirmed on this biopsy, and correlation with thoracic imaging is recommended. If a lung primary is confirmed, the multiple hepatic metastases would correspond to M1c and stage IVB under AJCC 8th edition. pT and pN cannot be assessed on core biopsy material.

errors.rationale: The diagnosis must be supported by the microscopic description.
